title: Peer failure taxonomy and fastest evidence path
mode: Primary-source project documentation and open issue review; research-only
scope: Compare peer handling of unknown DWG classes and route-specific test organization.
Review current peer parser failure reports for bounded-progress and record-isolation lessons.
Refine the local implementation plan's per-slice test selection without increasing validation cadence.

sources.revision: Current primary documentation/source pages reviewed 2026-10-19; no commit hash pinned or project executed.
sources.observed: The manual says unhandled classes/invalid types are non-critical and unknown types may be stored as binary blobs without DXF codes. CMake registers shell converter tests and unit tests separately. HACKING describes dedicated parser fuzz routes.
sources.limitation: Unknown binary preservation is not typed support or necessarily DXF re-emission. Test architecture is a project design observation, not evidence that any peer result qualifies libdxfrw.

sources.revision: Current repository and setup documentation reviewed 2026-10-19; no package checksum/source commit resolved or executed.
sources.observed: The README declares named ASCII/Binary DXF version support and read-only legacy inputs that are upgraded on write. Test instructions separate tests and integration_tests. The project is DXF-specific, not a DWG codec or ACIS kernel.
sources.limitation: A broad DXF matrix does not supply DWG coverage or independent solid semantics. Same-library readback is not independent evidence.

sources.revision: Issue bodies reviewed 2026-10-19. #1281 identifies 3.8.0 and says affected code remains on master; #1279 identifies 3.8.0 and says the same code is on master. No peer code or input was downloaded/run.
sources.observed: #1281 reports stack exhaustion from recursive advancement over repeated comments, XDATA app blocks, and WIPEOUT clip groups. #1279 reports whole-file failure on an AC1014 POLYLINE with VERTEX records containing AcDbVertex but no more-specific subtype marker.
sources.limitation: These are peer-reported shapes and versions, not reproduced behavior here or format rules. Reported byte/item thresholds and the proposed parent-based type inference are not normative.

assessment.planImpact: Adds an implementation-ready local test-selection sequence and explicit evidence distinctions for unknown-class retention, parser progress, record isolation, writer completeness, strict reopen, semantics, and native acceptance. Existing owners and validation cadence remain unchanged.

implementationReadiness: Use a tiny locally generated parser control with a suffix sentinel; test both encodings only when they share the changed path.
For adapter changes, assert ownership closure, callback isolation, rollback, and retry only where promised by the operation contract.
For writers, assert target-version framing and per-source disposition before strict local reopen; successful exit and entity count are not completeness proofs.
Pin one independent peer/native route only at its existing composed checkpoint for a claim that requires independence.
Reserve sanitizer/fuzz and broad suite execution for planned composed checkpoints, except when a slice directly changes the relevant security boundary.
Do not copy peer crash thresholds or infer malformed-record type from container context without authoritative format support.

method.kind: Read-only primary-source documentation and issue review plus local plan crosswalk
method.limitations: Issue reports and repository documentation can change and were not reproduced. External observations remain advisory and cannot promote local or DEFERRED_EXTERNAL support rows.
